subject: Privinfra: credentials handling and bastion pattern for VPC-connected on-prem nodes

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 07 Feb 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Privinfra: credentials handling and bastion pattern for VPC-connected on-prem nodes

Team — kicking off a narrow IaC review focused on two tightly scoped questions for the ACME private deployment:

1) How we manage machine identity and bootstrap credentials for on-prem hosts that will join the VPC-connected cluster (Terraform + Ansible flow).
2) Recommended bastion/egress pattern and how that maps to Helm values for the gateway components (how to keep admin access auditable and off the public internet).

Background: ACME is preparing to run a Redwood Private stack in their co-lo with a VPC peering link. They want a deterministic, reviewable IaC pattern — Terraform for infra, Ansible for host bootstrap, Helm for control-plane values. Security wants explicit guidance on ephemeral creds, KMS integration, and a non-shared bastion design.

Attached: priv-iac-review-checklist.pdf (checklist + acceptance criteria), vpc-onprem-network-diagram.png, bastion-ssh-patterns.md (notes from ACME infra).

Ask: can each of you review the checklist and call out any IaC gaps we should require as gating items for the GitLab pipelines? I'm particularly worried about:
- where secrets get written during bootstrap (local disk vs. ephemeral memory)
- Terraform remote state access from on-prem CI/CD runners
- operator access model (single central bastion vs. per-team jumpboxes)

I'll consolidate and send to Sam and their security team by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks —
Priya

Subject: Re: Privinfra: credentials handling and bastion pattern for VPC-connected on-prem nodes

Thanks Priya — quick notes after scanning the checklist and the diagram. Inline below.

> - where secrets get written during bootstrap (local disk vs. ephemeral memory)
We should require that bootstrap secrets are never persisted to disk in plaintext. Our recommendation: use an Ansible vault that pulls a short-lived cert from the customer's KMS via an agent installed on the bastion, then uses tmpfs for any ephemeral files. Add a Terraform null_resource that triggers cleanup hooks. I'll add a sample task in bastion-ops role.

> - Terraform remote state access from on-prem CI/CD runners
If the runner lives in customer network, we must avoid granting it direct write access to the managed state bucket. Instead: enforce a pipeline pattern where the runner obtains a short-lived token via an OIDC workflow against the customer's IdP (documented in checklist), and the remote state backend has a least-privilege RA policy. Also include a documented path for a 'bridge' runner in our Hosted control plane for emergency operations (with audit logging).

> - operator access model (single central bastion vs. per-team jumpboxes)
Recommend per-team bastions scoped to subnet + IAM roles (each with distinct SSH CA-issued certs) rather than a single shared box. That reduces blast radius and maps to Helm values: bastion.enabled=true, bastion.perTeam=true, bastion.sshCA: <url>. I will attach a tiny playbook that rotates the CA every 90 days.

I'll prepare a short diff for the checklist and add a sample Ansible role by EOD Monday.

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

- ACME will provide a KMS instance that supports short-lived signing keys and OIDC endpoints. We prefer to avoid installing any third-party agent inside our secure vault. Is the OIDC + short-lived token approach you described compatible with our KMS?

- For network egress: we need an audited egress path for telemetry (S3-like object storage). Can the bastions terminate TLS and forward telemetry via a dedicated egress subnet? We'll need the Helm values for the telemetry-gateway to pin outbound IPs.

- We want the ability to do offline bootstrap (air-gapped) for a subset of nodes. How much of the Terraform/Ansible flow relies on internet access to Redwood-hosted services?

If you can include small examples for the OIDC claims we should expect and a Helm values snippet for telemetry egress and bastion.sshCA, we can validate with our security team tomorrow.

Sam

Subject: Re: Privinfra: credentials handling and bastion pattern for VPC-connected on-prem nodes

Sam — quick answers and examples inline.

1) OIDC + KMS compatibility: yes. The OIDC flow we recommend is: runner authenticates to customer's IdP -> exchanges ID token with Redwood Token Broker (optional) -> broker mints short-lived AWS-style STS creds scoped to Terraform state operations. For customers that reject external brokers, we include a documented alternative to run the broker inside the customer's VPC (chart: token-broker helm template). Example OIDC claim we require: {"sub": "pipeline:acme/team-a:runner-42", "aud": "redwood-token-broker", "exp": 170? } (we'll provide exact schema in the doc).

2) Helm values example (telemetry egress + SSH CA):
- telemetry.gateway.enabled: true
- telemetry.gateway.egressSubnet: 10.200.254.0/26
- telemetry.gateway.outboundIPs: ["203.0.113.45"]
- bastion.enabled: true
- bastion.perTeam: true
- bastion.sshCAUrl: "https://kms.acmeinfra.com/ssh-ca/pk"

We will add this snippet to the checklist under the Helm values section and include a small chart override example for air-gapped installs (use imagePullSecrets + local registry mirror).

3) Air-gapped bootstrap: core Terraform modules can run fully offline if modules/artifacts are vendored into an on-prem artifact registry. Ansible playbooks should operate from local artifact bundles as well. We should add a gating item: CI job that validates artifact bundle integrity (signed tarball) before applying.

I'll push a small PR to the Drive folder with the exact OIDC sample and Helm snippet by EOD.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps.

Summary of gating items for the GitLab pipelines (to be added as checklist fails if missing):
- Terraform: remote state backend with OIDC-based short-lived creds; state encryption + drift detector job; remote-state write access only via scoped pipeline role.
- Ansible: no secrets written plaintext to disk; use vault + tmpfs; signed artifact bundle for playbooks used in air-gap scenarios.
- Helm: explicit values for telemetry egress IPs and bastion.sshCAUrl; chart override for local registry.
- Bastion/operator access: per-team bastion with SSH CA certs rotated every 90 days; audit logs shipped to customer-controlled S3 with lifecycle retention.

Action items:
- Mina: add Ansible role sample and a cleanup hook by Mon 2027-02-14.
- Irene: drop exact OIDC claim JSON and Helm snippet into Drive and link to JIRA INFRA-1248 by Tue 2027-02-09 (Irene already uploaded initial draft).
- Priya: finalize the checklist with gating language and send to Sam+security by Tue EOD.

Sam — once we have your confirmation on the outbound IPs and whether you want the broker hosted inside your VPC (option A) or allow Redwood token-broker (option B), we will mark the checklist ready for ACME's security review.

I'll create the JIRA ticket and link these docs. Closing this thread for now — please update the ticket as you complete the action items.

Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
